title: Contextual Savings Helper & Risk Annotator for batching + caching UI
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an interactive UI component for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-route batching + caching recommendations as a contextual ‘Savings Helper’ and highlights model-output risk with an inline ‘Risk Annotator’. The component should let operators preview expected token-cost delta, latency impact, and a short natural-language explanation of the trade-off. It must also mark prompts or routes where cache/prefill could change output semantics and offer a safe rollback path. This ticket focuses on the design prototype, microcopy, and acceptance criteria; engineering integration and API schema are handled in an adjacent ENG ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows a per-route Savings Helper panel with: baseline cost, estimated cost after recommendation, estimated p50/p95 latency change, and a 2-3 sentence summary of the trade-off.
Risk Annotator flags examples where prefix caching or aggressive batching may alter outputs and provides an explainable reason (e.g., 'prefix token overlap detected; possible context truncation').
Interactive slider for 'aggressiveness' updates cost/latency estimates live and updates the annotated risk level.
Preview mode runs 3 sample prompts (configurable) and shows diffed output snippets with highlighted changes; each diff links to eval run results in the dashboard.
Design tokens, color semantics, and iconography follow Console style guide; accessibility: color contrast and ARIA labels validated.
Final Figma prototype contains documented states for: default, recommended-on, user-overrode-recommendation, rollback-suggested, and blocked-by-policy.
Hand-off notes and a short spec (1 page) posted to Confluence with API contract link and QA checklist.
design_notes: Core idea: lower the cognitive load for platform owners by surfacing an actionable, explainable recommendation rather than raw knobs. The Savings Helper lives in the per-route config panel alongside existing batching/cache toggles. It should compute and display three primary signals: cost delta (tokens/time-interval), latency delta (p50/p95), and risk level (none/low/medium/high). The Risk Annotator is conservative: it runs a lightweight static analysis against the prompt set and flags constructs sensitive to prefix caching (e.g., dynamic user-specific prefixes, instructions that include user tokens) and batching (e.g., reliance on response order). Provide microcopy to explain why something is flagged and recommended mitigations (use stronger prompt anchors, move sensitive fields outside cacheable prefix, decrease batch size). The slider is labeled 'Economy vs Fidelity' with 5 discrete steps; each step maps to a precomputed profile (safe, balanced, aggressive) defined by runtime heuristics. Use an inline mini-simulator to show 3 example outputs with diffs and a 'confidence' badge that ties back to eval metrics. Prioritize clear rollback affordances: 'preview changes', 'apply to canary', 'revert to last stable'.
review_comments: 2026-03-06 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Love the slider approach. Request: include explicit canary rollout CTA and a small explainer of canary traffic sizing.
2026-03-08 - Rafael Ortiz (Eng): Backend can emit per-route simulation results; need a stable schema. Suggest we include an example payload in the spec before handoff.
2026-03-10 - Anya Li (Design): Iterated microcopy to reduce jargon; changed 'prefix-sensitive' to 'may depend on user-specific input' for clarity.
2026-03-12 - Security (Samir Patel): Flagged that risk annotations must not log sample user content; recommend using hashed examples or synthetic prompts in previews.
2026-03-13 - QA (Jordan Miles): Suggested accessibility checks and keyboard flow for the slider and preview diffs; noted color contrast issues in step 4 (aggressive).
decisions: Keep slider at 5 steps (Safe, Slight, Balanced, Aggressive, Maximum) — maps to runtime profiles maintained by ENG.
Preview diffs will use synthetic or redacted examples by default to avoid PII leakage; customer can opt-in to use real examples with audit logging enabled.
Risk Annotator will expose only a short natural-language rationale plus a severity; avoid exposing low-level static analysis rules to end users.
Include 'Apply to canary' and 'Apply to all' primary buttons; default is canary with recommended 5% traffic unless overridden by the user.
